successors.name: House of Bourbon
successors.text: the lands of Henry II of Navarre as count of Foix (Foix, Béarn, Bigorre and Albret), which pass to his daughter Jeanne III and her husband Antoine de Bourbon on 25 May 1555; Cliopatria's House of…

ledger.x: c. 1034: the county of Foix begins on the Ariège lands detached from the county of Carcassonne. 'The title of count of Foix was first assumed by Roger of Foix (died ca. 1064)', who inherited 'the town of Foix and the adjoining lands'; the infobox dates the county to the 'Mid-11th Century'. The List of counts of Foix…
8 September 1278: Roger-Bernard III and the Bishop of Urgell conclude the paréage that makes the counts of Foix co-princes of Andorra.
1290: the court moves west to Orthez, the capital of Béarn.
27 November 1379: Bigorre cedes to Gaston III.
5 January 1390: Gaston III gives Bigorre up.
1391: Gaston III dies without a legitimate heir and the line passes to Matthew of Foix-Castelbon.
1407: John I of Foix buys Bigorre.
1464: the court moves from Orthez to Pau.
1484: the Albret line joins the Foix inheritance.
1484: the Périgord and Limousin lands of the Albret line join the composite.
1484: the Albret lordship joins the composite (Lot-et-Garonne and the Gironde and Lot cells of the Cliopatria shape).
1507: Gaston de Foix gives Narbonne to Louis XII.
25 May 1555: Henry II of Navarre dies and his lands pass to Jeanne III and Antoine de Bourbon.

wars.name: Revolt of the count of Foix against Philip III
wars.outcome: The king besieged Foix on 3 June; the conflict was resolved on 8 February 1273 and the count, released, did homage to the king of France before the end of the year.

wars.name: Revolt of Roger-Bernard III against Peter of Aragon
wars.outcome: Roger-Bernard rose in open rebellion in spring 1280, surrendered on 22 July and was imprisoned until December 1283, freed 'in exchange for the viscounty of Castelbon'.

wars.name: Foix-Armagnac war over Béarn
wars.outcome: In 1293 Gerard V of Armagnac 'contested the usurpation of Béarn and began a long war'; 'This war lasted until 1377.'

wars.name: Treaty of Brétigny settlement for Bigorre
wars.outcome: The treaty of 8 May 1360 left Bigorre to others and Gaston III received 'a cash payout of 200,000 guilders' for its loss.

wars.name: War of Comminges
wars.outcome: The Count of Comminges died on 15 October 1375; after the battle at Cazères-sur-l'Adour in November 1376, the agreement of Barcelonne-du-Gers (3 April 1379) gave Gaston III the Mauvezin and Goudon castellanies.

certainty.note: Seigneurial frontiers between the Pyrenean counties, Béarn, Armagnac and Comminges are approximate, and nothing outlines the county before Cliopatria's 1236 shape; the line of the Pyrenees against Aragon and Navarre is firm, but no datable…
